@calvin0327 thank you for looking into this. After giving it some more thought, I'd like to propose an alternative approach, which is implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107698. That proposes a larger change, but has stronger guarantees that the overridden checks are only skipped when the overriding check is present. It also allows for versioned overrides, in case a baseline check predates an overriding restricted check.

issue_context.title: [PodSecurity] Dedupe overlapping forbidden messages
issue_context.body:
Examples:
* restricted volumes complains about hostPath volumes already caught by baseline hostPath check
* restricted capabilities complains about added non-default capabilities already caught by baseline capabilities check
* restricted seccomp complains about unconfined seccomp profile already caught by baseline seccomp check
comments: @liggitt does this issue need help, I would like to collaborate. Could you please elaborate about what we are trying to achieve here.

With the current implementation, baseline checks and restricted checks are run independently

Some baseline and restricted checks overlap in what they check (examples in the issue description), such that the restricted check enforces everything the baseline check does and more.

A pod submitted to a restricted namespace that fails both checks will get two errors returned, when it really only needs one. A good example is submitting a pod that uses a hostPath volume to a restricted namespace. It will fail the [restrictedVolumes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/pod-security-admission/policy/check_restrictedVolumes.go) check and the [hostPathVolumes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/pod-security-admission/policy/check_hostPathVolumes.go) checks.

We'd like to just return one error in that case, but that requires making independent checks aware of each other, and adding short-circuiting logic to skip the baseline checks when the corresponding restricted check is done, which entangles those a bit.

review_comments:
marking checks as overlapping and skipping them without positive verification that the specific check they overlap with is also getting run makes me slightly nervous

the integration test failures are related, and make it seem like some expected checks aren't getting run
